entries.content_plain:
CHAPTER 26
 
Ex 26:1-37. Ten Curtains

1. cunning work--that is, of elegant texture, richly embroidered. The word "cunning," in old English, is synonymous with "skilful."
entries.reader_content_plain: 1. cunning work--that is, of elegant texture, richly embroidered. The word "cunning," in old English, is synonymous with "skilful."

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv862"/><div sID="gen1197" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv862"/><hi type="bold">15-30. thou shalt make boards ... rear up the tabernacle according to the fashion ... which was showed thee--</hi>The tabernacle, from its name as well as from its general appearance and arrangements, was a tent; but from the description given in these verses, the boards that formed its walls, the five (cross) bars that strengthened them, and the middle bar that "reached from end to end," and gave it solidity and compactness, it was evidently a more substantial fabric than a light and fragile tent, probably on account of the weight of its various coverings as well as for the protection of its precious furniture. <div eID="gen1197" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv863"/><div sID="gen1198" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv863"/><hi type="bold">36. an hanging for the door of the tent--</hi>Curtains of rich and elaborate embroidery, made by the women, are suspended over the doors or entrances of the tents occupied by Eastern chiefs and princes. In a similar style of elegance was the hanging finished which was to cover the door of this tabernacle--the chosen habitation of the God and King of Israel. It appears from <reference osisRef="Exod.26.12">Ex 26:12</reference>, <reference osisRef="Exod.22.23">22, 23</reference>, that the ark and mercy seat were placed in the west end of the tabernacle, and consequently the door or entrance fronted the east, so that the Israelites in worshipping Jehovah, turned their faces towards the west; that they might be thus figuratively taught to turn from the worship of that luminary which was the great idol of the nations, and to adore the God who made it and them [Hewlett]. <chapter eID="Exod.26"/>
